entries.claim: fixes-boundary does not tell the finding's loans/repairs boundary apart from an unrelated edit, because the seeded spine's S-03 (Reminders run from a daily scheduled job) is already a `Kind: boundaries` decision that says 'reads the loan log'. Adding the word 'repair' anywhere in S-03 satisfies all three lookaheads. The same grader is byte-copied into readiness-fix-answer.
entries.failure_scenario: Start from samples/readiness/spine.md and change only S-03's body to 'A job runs once a day, reads the loan log and the repair log and sends that day's reminders.' Run the grader's pattern over that file and it matches at '## S-03: Reminders run from a daily scheduled job' (checked with node). That edit draws no boundary between loans and repairs, and E-02 still crosses them. Yet edits-spine, no-epics-*, ends-on-confirm and fixes-boundary all pass, and the stale check still reports the epics as stale, so readiness-fix scores 1.00. This contradicts PLAN-6 Task 4's claim that an edit that 'changes something else' fails it. The risk is concrete in readiness-fix-answer: its route edits S-03 (kept trace readiness-fix-answer-try-2 writes the who-relies answer there), so a run that adds a repair mention to S-03 instead of adding the S-07 boundary would also pass.
